messages:
Maria: FYI CI is flagging the schema-lint job for audit events after the KMS key rotation this morning. Failing in the validation harness, not obvious why yet.
Alex: on it. Which test suite? goldenset or the live contract checks?
Maria: the goldenset comparison in the validation harness (goldenset-schema-lint). It fails with a missing 'actor.id' in a handful of customer-facing audit events.
Chris: I pulled the raw event from the canary here — looks like redaction changed to 'actor': {"type": "service", "id": null} instead of removing the key. Validator expects string id.
Chris: snippet: ```json
{"event":"key.access","actor":{"type":"service","id":null},"target":{"resource":"kms/key/123"}}
```
Jen: ah that matches the KMS rotation change we shipped — we changed the redaction behavior to emit a typed actor stub for privacy. Tests didn't get updated.
Alex: ideally the validator should allow actor.id to be missing OR null when actor.type == "service"; customer-facing audit schema must be explicit about nullability.
Maria: agreed. Two paths: (A) patch the goldenset to reflect new stub, or (B) make validator more permissive for this field. Which do we prefer?
Chris: for fast unblock in CI, patch the goldenset with the new stub. But long-term we should tighten the schema and add a note for downstream customers.
Jen: +1. I'll make a small PR to the golden fixtures. Also adding a unit test that simulates key rotation redaction so we don't regress.
ops-bot: deploy pipeline triggered for branch: jen/kms-redaction-golden-fix — stage: integration
Alex: heads-up: if we just change goldenset, we might hide an upstream bug where an actual actor.id got dropped unexpectedly. Recommend adding an assertion in the validator harness that logs when id == null for non-service actor types.
Maria: good catch. Add that as a soft warning for now — we don't want CI to be red for legitimate user-facing mistakes but we do want telemetry.
Chris: I'll add a telemetry counter and a debug log line: `audit.validator.null_actor_id` with actor.type and event name. That should surface in datadog.
security-bot: Alert created: SEC-1128 — "Audit event actor.id null occurrences post-KMS-rotation" assigned to Maria, priority: P3
Jen: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-fixtures/pull/82 — updates goldenset and adds rotation unit test. CI rerun in ~5m.
Maria: rerun passed for the goldenset job but the contract-check job still fails on a different event where `actor` is a string (legacy) and not an object. Looks like two variants in the wild.
Alex: Ugh. We need a compatibility layer in the validator: accept actor as string OR object with optional id field. Document in schema as union: string | {type: string, id?: string|null}.
Chris: I'll sketch the validator change today. It will emit structured normalize() output so downstream consumers always get object form.
Maria: timeline: patch goldenset to unblock, then submit validator change + schema note, then update release notes and notify PSG/customer success if customers consume raw audit events.
Jen: cc @product-observability — we should update the audit event contract doc and add migration notes for customers.
Alex: also check RBAC changes that shipped with the rotation — make sure actor role claims weren't dropped in some code path. Might be a separate bug.
Maria: creating follow-up ticket SEC-1129 for RBAC claim audit. For now the CI unblock approach stands. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
